The evidence explicitly contrasts the two methods. It states that the Pixel Shader Fragment Clipping method 'rasterizes the full triangle to all intersecting slices and clips in the pixel shader' (Source S1, Section 3.2 and notes), whereas the Geometry Shader Slicing method 'performs clipping in the geometry shader, generating strips for each slice' (Source S1, notes). Furthermore, the evidence notes that the pixel shader method 'produces many fragments that are rejected in the pixel shader, which can be an issue' on architectures with small bandwidth or intensive pixel shader usage, and that the geometry shader approach is 'favored here because it produces exactly the fragments rasterized in the final volume slices' (Source S1, notes). This supports the claim that the geometry shader approach avoids fragment rejection overhead and is suitable for such architectures.
